sections.title: 听力
sections.instructions: 录音只播一遍。25 题单选，每题 9.94 分（710 分制，听力共 248.5 分）。

parts.zh: W: 我一直在想，今年夏天
M: 露营车？你的意思是整个夏天都住在车里？
M: 我觉得我爷爷以前就有一辆那样的车
W: 现在的露营车完全不一样了
M: 我开始有点接受这个想法了
W: 现在有很多人全职投入这种生活方式
M: 好吧，我们可以考虑一下
W: 别急。很高兴你这么兴奋
M: 听着，你在我们这儿工作快五年了

questions.stem: What has the woman been thinking of doing for this summer?
options: Renting a car instead of driving their own.
Surfing online to check out the best deals.
Exploring more summer holiday resorts.
Spending their holidays in a novel way.
optionsZh: 租一辆车而不是开他们自己的车。
在网上浏览以查看最优惠的价格。
探索更多的避暑度假胜地。
以一种新颖的方式度过假期。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：Spending their holidays in a novel way.（以一种新颖的方式度过假期。）

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man's grandfather from the conversation?
options: He once owned a van.
He was well travelled.
He did not find holiday homes appealing.
He did not like to be locked into one place.
optionsZh: 他曾经拥有一辆面包车。
他去过很多地方旅行。
他觉得度假屋没有吸引力。
他不喜欢被限制在一个地方。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：He once owned a van.（他曾经拥有一辆面包车。）

questions.stem: What can many camper vans do nowadays according to the woman?
options: Ensure the safety of passengers.
Drive under any weather condition.
Receive instructions via computers.
Generate their own electricity.
optionsZh: 确保乘客的安全。
在任何天气条件下行驶。
通过计算机接收指令。
自行发电。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：Generate their own electricity.（自行发电。）

questions.stem: What idea does the woman find attractive?
options: Having one's basic needs covered while away from home.
Enjoying the freedom to choose where to go and work.
Slowing down in one's increasingly hectic life.
Riding one's mountain bike on vacation.
optionsZh: 离家在外时基本需求得到满足。
享有选择去哪里和在哪里工作的自由。
在日益忙碌的生活中放慢节奏。
度假时骑山地自行车。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：Enjoying the freedom to choose where to go and work.（享有选择去哪里和在哪里工作的自由。）

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman from the man's description?
options: She has missed several important appointments lately.
Her job performance has worsened over the past month.
She has lagged behind most of her co-workers in output.
Her physical health has deteriorated these past few weeks.
optionsZh: 她最近错过了几个重要的约会。
她过去一个月的工作表现变差了。
她的产出落后于大多数同事。
她过去几周的身体健康状况恶化了。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：Her job performance has worsened over the past month.（她过去一个月的工作表现变差了。）

questions.stem: What does the woman say she's experiencing at the moment?
options: Serious health issues.
Disturbance of her mind.
Some problems at home.
Penalty for curtailed output.
optionsZh: 严重的健康问题。
精神上的困扰。
家里的一些问题。
因产出减少而受到的处罚。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：Some problems at home.（家里的一些问题。）

questions.stem: What does the man say makes his job far easier?
options: The woman's work proficiency.
The woman's whole-hearted support.
His engaging personality.
His management capability.
optionsZh: 女士的工作能力。
女士的全心全意支持。
他有吸引力的个性。
他的管理能力。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：The woman's work proficiency.（女士的工作能力。）

questions.stem: What agreement have the speakers reached by the end of the conversation?
options: The woman will resume her work in two weeks.
The man will be back at his 100% in a couple of weeks.
The woman will be off work on the next two Mondays.
The man will help the woman get back to her usual self.
optionsZh: 女士将在两周后恢复工作。
男士将在几周内恢复到百分之百的状态。
女士接下来两个星期一将休假。
男士将帮助女士恢复到她平常的状态。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：The woman will be off work on the next two Mondays.（女士接下来两个星期一将休假。）

questions.stem: What does research suggest about a higher level of education?
options: It can have an impact on our moods and emotions.
It can enable us to live a healthier and longer life.
It can improve our financial status significantly.
It can help us achieve better work performance.
optionsZh: 它可以影响我们的心境和情绪。
它可以使我们过上更健康、更长寿的生活。
它可以显著改善我们的经济状况。
它可以帮助我们取得更好的工作表现。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：It can enable us to live a healthier and longer life.（它可以使我们过上更健康、更长寿的生活。）

questions.stem: What do we learn from the finding of the new research?
options: One's health tends to differ before and after marriage.
One's health status is related to one's social background.
The wealthier one's spouse is, the healthier one becomes.
The spouse's level of education can impact one's health.
optionsZh: 一个人的健康状况在婚前和婚后往往有所不同。
一个人的健康状况与其社会背景有关。
配偶越富有,一个人就越健康。
配偶的教育水平可以影响一个人的健康。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：The spouse's level of education can impact one's health.（配偶的教育水平可以影响一个人的健康。）

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the men in the sample of the new research?
options: They benefited a lot from their career achievements.
They showed interest in their spouse's occupations.
They had much in common with their spouses.
They had more education than their spouses.
optionsZh: 他们从自己的职业成就中受益匪浅。
他们对配偶的职业表现出兴趣。
他们与配偶有很多共同点。
他们比配偶受过更多教育。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：They had more education than their spouses.（他们比配偶受过更多教育。）

questions.stem: What is said to be a key challenge for cities prone to floods?
options: Eliminating their root cause.
Forecasting flood risks accurately.
Identifying the cities' geological features.
Finding out the changing climate patterns.
optionsZh: 消除洪水的根本原因。
准确预测洪水风险。
识别城市的地质特征。
找出不断变化的气候模式。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：Forecasting flood risks accurately.（准确预测洪水风险。）

questions.stem: For what purpose does Derek Loftis collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides?
options: To validate his hypothesis about the gravity of floods.
To determine the frequency of high tides causing floods.
To improve his mathematical flooding model.
To see the feasibility of his project on flooding.
optionsZh: 验证他关于洪水严重程度的假设。
确定引发洪水的大潮发生频率。
改进他的洪水数学模型。
了解他的洪水项目的可行性。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：To improve his mathematical flooding model.（改进他的洪水数学模型。）

questions.stem: What does the passage say is Derek Loftis's mission?
options: To study the consequences of high tides on flooded areas.
To teach local citizens how to collect data of incoming floods.
To forecast rapid floods in real time.
To classify the flooding data processed.
optionsZh: 研究大潮对洪水淹没地区的后果。
教当地市民如何收集即将到来的洪水的数据。
实时预报快速洪水。
对处理过的洪水数据进行分类。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：To forecast rapid floods in real time.（实时预报快速洪水。）

questions.stem: What did Loftis and his colleagues do to obtain data about water height and movement?
options: They set up Internet-connected water-level sensors.
They tracked the rising tides with video-cameras.
They used newly-developed supercomputing facilities.
They observed the direction of water flow on the spot.
optionsZh: 他们安装了联网的水位传感器。
他们用摄像机追踪涨潮情况。
他们使用了新开发的超级计算设施。
他们现场观察水流方向。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：They set up Internet-connected water-level sensors.（他们安装了联网的水位传感器。）

questions.stem: What does the speaker say has become something of a ritual?
options: To argue about the value of a college degree.
To debate the validity of current survey data.
To account for the drastic decline in employment among men.
To compare men without college degrees with those who have.
optionsZh: 争论大学学位的价值。
辩论当前调查数据的有效性。
解释男性就业急剧下降的原因。
将没有大学学位的男性与有大学学位的男性进行比较。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：To argue about the value of a college degree.（争论大学学位的价值。）

questions.stem: What did the researchers of a recent working paper consider first?
options: The increase in women taking up jobs.
The issue of changing job requirements.
The factor of wages.
The impact of inflation.
optionsZh: 女性从事工作的增加。
工作要求变化的问题。
工资因素。
通货膨胀的影响。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：The factor of wages.（工资因素。）

questions.stem: What did the recent paper identify as a new potential explanation of the problem concerning men's employment?
options: Men's unwillingness to accept low wages in times of growing inflation.
The wage gap between those with college degrees and those without.
More jobs requiring their holders to have a college degree nowadays.
The sharp decline in marriage among men with no college degrees.
optionsZh: 男性在通货膨胀加剧时期不愿接受低工资。
有大学学位者与无大学学位者之间的工资差距。
如今更多工作要求持有者拥有大学学位。
没有大学学位的男性结婚率急剧下降。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：The sharp decline in marriage among men with no college degrees.（没有大学学位的男性结婚率急剧下降。）

questions.stem: What has a market research team found in its latest fashion and sustainability report?
options: More and more people attach importance to protecting endangered animals.
More and more people prioritize animal welfare when buying things to wear.
An increasing number of people demand to free animals being kept in cages.
An increasing number of people follow the latest trend of becoming vegetarians.
optionsZh: 越来越多的人重视保护濒危动物。
越来越多的人在购买穿戴物品时优先考虑动物福利。
越来越多的人要求释放被关在笼子里的动物。
越来越多的人追随成为素食主义者的最新潮流。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：More and more people prioritize animal welfare when buying things to wear.（越来越多的人在购买穿戴物品时优先考虑动物福利。）

questions.stem: What have some world-renowned fashion designers done for some time?
options: Avoided the use of leather and fur.
Labelled all their products as vegan.
Refrained from using chemicals in their products.
Utilized a silk substitute made from mushrooms.
optionsZh: 避免使用皮革和毛皮。
将他们所有的产品标注为纯素产品。
避免在产品中使用化学物质。
使用由蘑菇制成的丝绸替代品。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：Avoided the use of leather and fur.（避免使用皮革和毛皮。）

questions.stem: What does the speaker say is unclear concerning vegan products?
options: Whether they actually signify a substantial change.
Whether they effectively protect animals at large.
Whether they can be considered sustainable.
Whether they can be regarded as ethical.
optionsZh: 它们是否真正标志着实质性的改变。
它们是否能有效地保护整体上的动物。
它们是否可以被认为是可持续的。
它们是否可以被视为符合伦理的。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：Whether they can be regarded as ethical.（它们是否可以被视为符合伦理的。）

questions.stem: What is one of the facts stated by the speaker?
options: The era we live in is the most peaceful in history.
The world has seen more violence in recent years.
The environmental welfare has worsened in the world.
The belief is less prevalent that the world is going to hell.
optionsZh: 我们生活的时代是历史上最和平的。
近年来世界上发生了更多暴力事件。
世界环境福祉已经恶化。
认为世界正在走向毁灭的观念不那么普遍了。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：The era we live in is the most peaceful in history.（我们生活的时代是历史上最和平的。）

questions.stem: What do we learn about most British and French people in a 2015 survey for YouGov?
options: They were actually not in their right mind.
They believed the world was deteriorating.
They did not wish to live in the previous century.
They were convinced by the statistics presented to them.
optionsZh: 他们实际上神智不清。
他们认为世界正在恶化。
他们不愿生活在上个世纪。
他们被呈现给他们的统计数据说服了。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：They believed the world was deteriorating.（他们认为世界正在恶化。）

questions.stem: What does our prevailing mood of despair indicate?
options: The subjectivity of mass media.
The current state of affairs.
Our psychological biases.
Our ancestors' influence.
optionsZh: 大众媒体的主观性。
当前的事态。
我们的心理偏见。
我们祖先的影响。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：Our psychological biases.（我们的心理偏见。）

questions.stem: What was a very good thing in our evolutionary past?
options: Spreading exciting news around us far and wide.
Vacuuming up depressing or enraging stories.
Calculating dangerous risks to our survival.
Paying attention to negative information.
optionsZh: 把令人兴奋的消息广泛传播到我们周围。
大量吸收令人沮丧或愤怒的故事。
计算对我们生存的危险风险。
关注负面信息。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：Paying attention to negative information.（关注负面信息。）

items.explain: 听力占 35%（248.5 分），25 题。录音只播一遍：先按原速听完整卷，再对答案。

sections.title: 写作
sections.instructions: 真题 Part Ⅰ · 30 分钟 · 150–210 词

items.prompt: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “Nowadays parents are increasingly aware that allowing kids more freedom to explore and learn on their own helps foster their independence and boost their confidence.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay.You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words(not including the sentence given).
items.rubric: CET 写作 15 分制（六级）：切题、篇章连贯、用词准确

sections.title: 选词填空
sections.instructions: 真题 Part Ⅲ Section A · 15 选 10 · 10 空

items.stem: Our brains respond to language expressing facts differently than they do to words conveying possibility, scientists at New York University have recently found. Their work offers new insights into the impact word choice has on how we {{1}} between statements expressing what is real versus what is merely possible. The researchers assert their findings are important because we are presented with false information all the time. Some of this is {{2}} , as is the case with deceptive advertisements, but the problem is {{3}} by individuals who believe they are sharing correct information. Thus, it is more important than ever to separate the factual from the possible or merely {{4}} in how we communicate. This is especially true as the study makes clear that information presented as fact {{5}} special responses in our brains, which are distinct from when we process the same content with clear indicators of {{6}} . In their new study, the scientists intended to {{7}} how the brain computes possibilities as expressed by words such as "may," "might," and "if." The researchers compared brain responses to statements expressing factual {{8}} and those expressing possibility. "There is a monster under my bed" exemplifies a factual statement. "I will stay home," is also factual. This is opposed to statements that express possibility, like "There might be a monster under my bed," or "If it rains, I will stay home." The results of the study showed that factual language {{9}} a rapid increase in brain activity, with the brain responding more powerfully and showing more engagement with factual phrases compared to those communicating possibility. Thus, facts rule when it comes to the brain. Brain regions involved in processing {{10}} rapidly distinguish facts from possibilities. Further, these regions respond in a much more robust fashion to factual statements.
options: activated
aggravated
ascertain
deliberate
differentiate
discourse
evokes
inhibit
manuscript
marvels
remnants
scenarios
speculative
unanimous
uncertainty
blankExplains:
【定位】Their work offers new insights into the impact word choice has on how we ____ between statements expressing what is real versus what is merely possible.
【依据】答案是 differentiate：填回后与所在句 work、offers、new、insights、into、impact 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】Some of this is ____ , as is the case with deceptive advertisements, but the problem is  … by individuals who believe they are sharing correct information.
【依据】答案是 deliberate：填回后与所在句 case、deceptive、advertisements、problem、individuals、who 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】Some of this is  … , as is the case with deceptive advertisements, but the problem is ____ by individuals who believe they are sharing correct information.
【依据】答案是 aggravated：填回后与所在句 case、deceptive、advertisements、problem、individuals、who 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】Thus, it is more important than ever to separate the factual from the possible or merely ____ in how we communicate.
【依据】答案是 speculative：填回后与所在句 thus、important、ever、separate、factual、possible 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】This is especially true as the study makes clear that information presented as fact ____ special responses in our brains, which are distinct from when we process the same content with clear indicators of  … .
【依据】答案是 evokes：填回后与所在句 especially、true、study、makes、clear、information 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】This is especially true as the study makes clear that information presented as fact  … special responses in our brains, which are distinct from when we process the same content with clear indicators of ____ .
【依据】答案是 uncertainty：填回后与所在句 especially、true、study、makes、clear、information 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】In their new study, the scientists intended to ____ how the brain computes possibilities as expressed by words such as "may," "might," and "if." The researchers compared brain responses to statements expressing factual  … and those expressing possibility.
【依据】答案是 ascertain：填回后与所在句 new、study、scientists、intended、how、brain 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】In their new study, the scientists intended to  … how the brain computes possibilities as expressed by words such as "may," "might," and "if." The researchers compared brain responses to statements expressing factual ____ and those expressing possibility.
【依据】答案是 scenarios：填回后与所在句 new、study、scientists、intended、how、brain 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】This is opposed to statements that express possibility, like "There might be a monster under my bed," or "If it rains, I will stay home." The results of the study showed that factual language ____ a rapid increase in brain activity, with the brain responding more powerfully and showing more engagement with factual phrases compared to those communicating possibility.
【依据】答案是 activated：填回后与所在句 opposed、statements、express、possibility、like、there 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】Brain regions involved in processing ____ rapidly distinguish facts from possibilities.
【依据】答案是 discourse：填回后与所在句 brain、regions、involved、processing、rapidly、distinguish 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。
items.explain: 本段为选词填空，共 10 空，候选词 15 个。解题顺序是：先通读判断体裁与话题 → 按词性给候选词分组 → 逐空用搭配与语义场排除。15 选 10 意味着有 5 个候选词永远用不上，遇到"读起来也通顺"的选项时要看它是否破坏了整段的一致性。

paragraphs.text: Most visitors come to Cape Canaveral, on the northeast coast of Florida, for the tourist attractions. It's home to the second-busiest cruise ship port in the world and is a gateway to the cosmos. Nearly 1.5 million visitors flock here every year to watch rockets, spacecraft, and satellites blast off into the solar system from Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex. Nearly 64 kilometers of undeveloped beach and 648 square kilometers of protected refuge fan out from the cape's sandy shores.

Yet some of Cape Canaveral's most legendary attractions lie unseen, wedged under the sea's surface in mud and sand, for this part of the world has a reputation as a deadly ship trap. Over the centuries, dozens of majestic Old World sailing ships smashed and sank on this irregular stretch of windy Florida coast. They were vessels built for war and commerce, crossing the globe carrying everything from coins to cannons, boxes of silver and gold, chests of jewels and porcelain, and pearls from the Caribbean.

Cape Canaveral contains one of the greatest concentrations of colonial shipwrecks in the world. In recent years, advances in radar, diving, detection equipment, computers, and GPS have transformed the hunt. The naked eye might see a pile of rocks, but technology can reveal the precious artifacts(人工制品) that lie hidden on the ocean floor.

As technology renders the seabed more accessible, the hunt for treasure-filled ships has drawn a fresh tide of salvors(打捞人员) and their investors—as well as marine archaeologists(考古学家) wanting to bring to light the lost relics. But of late, when salvors have found vessels, their rights have been challenged in court. The big question: who should have control of these treasures?

High-stakes fights over shipwrecks pit archaeologists against treasure hunters in a vicious cycle of accusations. Archaeologists regard themselves as protectors of history, and they see salvors as careless destroyers. Salvors feel they do the hard work of searching for ships, only to have them stolen from under them when discovered. This kind of clash inevitably takes place on a grand scale. Aside from the salvors, their investors, and the maritime archaeologists who serve as expert witnesses, the battles sweep in local and international governments and organizations like UNESCO that work to protect under-water heritage. The court cases that ensue stretch on for years. Are finders keepers, or do the ships belong to the countries that made them and sent them sailing centuries ago? Where once salvors and archaeologists worked side by side, now they belong to opposing, and equally contemptuous, tribes.

Nearly three million vessels lie wrecked on the Earth's ocean floor—from old canoes to the Titanic—and likely less than one percent have been explored. Some—like an ancient Roman ship found off Antikythera, Greece, dated between 70 and 60 BC and carrying astonishingly sophisticated gears and dials for navigating by the sun—are critical to a new understanding of our past. No wonder there is an eternal stirring among everybody from salvors to scholars to find them.

In May 2016, a salvor named Bobby Pritchett, president of Global Marine Exploration (GME) in Tampa, Florida, announced that he had discovered scattered remains of a ship buried a kilometer off Cape Canaveral. Over the prior three years, he and his crew had obtained 14 state permits to survey a nearly 260-square-kilometer area off the cape; they worked 250 days a year, backed by investor funds of, he claims, US $4 million. It was hard work. Crew members were up at dawn, dragging sensors from their expedition vessels back and forth, day in and day out, year after year, to detect metal of any kind. Using computer technology, Pritchett and his crew created intricate, color-coded maps marked with the GPS coordinates of thousands of finds, all invisible under a meter of sand.

One day in 2015, the magnetometer(磁力计) picked up metal that turned out to be an iron cannon; when the divers blew the sand away, they also discovered a more precious bronze cannon with markings indicating French royalty and, not far off, a famous marble column carved with the coat of arms of France, known from historical paintings. The discovery was cause for celebration. The artifacts indicated the divers had likely found the wreck of La Trinité, a 16th-century French vessel that had been at the center of a bloody battle between France and Spain that changed the fate of the United States of America.

And then the legal storm began, with GME and Pritchett pitted against Florida and France. The Sunken Military Craft Act of 2004, a US federal act, protects any vessel that was on a military mission, allowing the originating country to claim their ship even centuries later. In 2018, two long years after Pritchett's discovery, the federal district court ruled in favor of France. For Pritchett, the decision was devastating. Millions of dollars of investor funding and years of labor were lost.

But this is far from the first time a salvor has lost all rights to a discovery. In 2012, for instance, Spain won a five-year legal battle against Odyssey Marine Exploration, which had hauled 594,000 gold and silver coins from a Spanish wreck off the coast of Portugal across the Atlantic to the United States. "Treasure hunters can be naive," says attorney David Concannon, who has had several maritime archaeologists as clients and represented two sides in the battles over the Titanic for 20 years. "Many treasure hunters don't understand they are going to have to fight for their rights against a government that has an endless supply of money for legal battles that treasure hunters are likely to lose."

Putting an inflated price on artifacts rather than viewing them as cultural and historical treasures that transcend any price is what irritates many archaeologists. For the archaeologist, everything in a wreck matters—hair, fabric, a fragment of a newspaper, rat bones-all things speak volumes. Archaeologists don't want artifacts ending up in a private collection instead of taking humanity on a journey of understanding.

George Bass is one of the pioneers of under-water archaeology, and a researcher at Texas A&M University. He has testified in court against treasure hunters, but says archaeology is not without its own serious problems. He believes archaeologists need to do a better job themselves instead of routinely criticizing treasure hunters. "Archaeology has a terrible reputation for not publishing enough on its excavations(发掘) and finds," he says. Gathering data, unearthing and meticulously preserving and examining finds, verifying identity and origin, piecing together the larger story, and writing and publishing a comprehensive paper or book can take decades. A bit cynically, Bass describes colleagues who never published because they waited so long they became ill or died. Who is more at fault, Bass asks, the professional archaeologist who carefully excavates a site and never publishes on it or the treasure hunter who locates a submerged wreck, salvages part, conserves part, and publishes a book on the operation?

Pritchett concedes that his find deserves careful excavation and preservation. "I think what I found should go in a museum," he says. "But I also think I should get paid for what I found." Indeed, it's a bit of a mystery why governments, archaeologists, and treasure hunters can't work together—and why salvors aren't at least given a substantial finder's fee before the original owner takes possession of the vessel and its artifacts.

items.passage: Could you get by without using the internet for four and a half years? That's exactly what singer and actress Selena Gomez has done in a bid to improve her mental health. She has spoken extensively about the relationship between her social media usage and her mental wellbeing, recalling feeling like "an addict" when she became Instagram's most followed user in 2016. "Taking a break from social media was the best decision that I've ever made for my mental health", says she. "The unnecessary hate and comparisons went away once I put my phone down." Ditching the web at large, however, is a far more subtle and complicated prospect. The increasing digitisation of our society means that everything from paying a gas bill to plotting a route to a friend's house and even making a phone call is at the mercy of your internet connection. Actively opting out of using the internet becomes a matter of privilege. Ms Gomez's multi-millionaire status has allowed her to take the "social" out of social media, so she can continue to leverage her enormous fame while keeping the trolls(恶意挑衅的帖子) at bay. The fact that she's still the second most-followed woman on Instagram suggests it's entirely possible to maintain a significant web profile to promote various projects—by way of a dedicated team—without being exposed to the cruel comments, hate mail and rape or death threats. It goes without saying that this is fundamentally different from how the rest of us without beauty deals and films to publicise use the likes of Instagram, TikTok and Twitter, but even the concept of a digital detox(戒瘾) requires having a device and connectivity to choose to disconnect from. The UK's digital divide has worsened over the past two years, leaving poorer families without broadband connections in their homes. Digital exclusion is a major threat to wider societal equality in the UK, so witnessing companies like Facebook championing the metaverse(元宇宙) as the next great frontier when school children are struggling to complete their homework feels particularly irritating. Consequently, it's worth bearing in mind that while deleting all social media accounts will undoubtedly make some feel infinitely better, many other people benefit from the strong sense of community that sharing platforms can breed. Internet access will continue to grow in importance as we edge further towards web 3.0, and greater resources and initiatives are needed to provide the underprivileged with the connectivity they desperately need to learn, work and live. It's crucial that people who feel that social media is having a detrimental effect on their mental health are allowed to switch off and for those living in digital exclusion to be able to switch on in the first place.

questions.stem: What do we learn about singer and actress Selena Gomez in the past four and a half years?
options: She has had worsening mental problems.
She has won Instagram's most followers.
She has refrained from using social media.
She has succeeded in a bid on the internet.

items.passage: Psychologists have long been in disagreement as to whether competition is a learned or a genetic component of human behavior. Whatever it is, you cannot but recognize the effect competition is exerting in academics and many other areas of contemporary life. Psychologically speaking, competition has been seen as an inevitable consequence of human drives. According to Sigmund Freud, humans are born screaming for attention and full of organic drives for fulfillment in various areas. Initially, we compete for the attention of our parents. Thereafter, we are at the mercy of a battle between our base impulses for self-fulfillment and social and cultural norms which prohibit pure indulgence. Current work in anthropology(人类学) has suggested, however, that this view of the role of competition in human behavior may be incorrect. Thomas Hobbes, one of the great philosophers of the seventeenth century, is perhaps best remembered for his characterization of the "natural world," that is, the world before the imposition of the will of humanity, as being "nasty, brutish, and short." This image of the pre-rational world is still widely held, reinforced by Charles Darwin's highly influential work, The Origin of Species, which established the doctrine of natural selection. This doctrine, which takes for granted that those species best able to adapt to and master the natural environment in which they live will survive, has suggested that the struggle for survival is an inherent human trait which determines a person's success. Darwin's theory has even been summarized as "survival of the fittest"—a phrase Darwin himself never used—further highlighting competition's role in success. As it has often been pointed out, however, there is nothing in the concept of natural selection that suggests that competition is the most successful strategy for "survival of the fittest." Darwin asserted in The Origin of Species that the struggles he was describing should be viewed as metaphors and could easily include dependence and cooperation. Many studies have been conducted to test the importance placed on competition as opposed to other values, such as cooperation—by various cultures, and generally conclude that Americans uniquely praise competition as natural, inevitable, and desirable. In 1937, the world-renowned anthropologist Margaret Mead published Cooperation and Competition among Primitive Peoples, based on her studies of several societies that did not prize competition, and, in fact, seemed at times to place a negative value on it. One such society was the Zuni Indians of Arizona, and they, Mead found, valued cooperation far more than competition. After studying dozens of such cultures, Mead's final conclusion was that competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior, and that its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it.

items.zh: 随着经济与社会的发展，中国人口结构发生了显著变化，逐渐步入老龄化社会。中国老年人口将持续增加，人口老龄化趋势将更加明显。为了应对人口老龄化带来的种种挑战，国家正积极采取措施，加大对养老的支持。通过改革社会保障制度，政府不断增加社会保障经费，逐步扩大社会保障覆盖范围，使更多老年人受益。政府还鼓励各种社会团体为老年人提供服务。在政府和社会团体的共同努力下，老年人将生活得更加幸福。
